item.title: Doolittle Raiders kin honor Sino-U.S. wartime friendship 84 years on
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
*Eighty-four years after the first U.S. air strike on the Japanese home islands during World War II, family members of some of the airmen traveled across the Pacific to retrace mountain paths where Chinese peasants risked torture and death to shelter downed American flyers, and to honor a friendship forged in wartime. *In April 1942, 16 U.S. bombers led by Lieutenant Colonel James Doolittle took off from the USS Hornet aircraft carrier to bomb Japan, in retaliation for the attack on Pearl Harbor. *After the operation, 15 planes heading for a designated airport in east China's Zhejiang Province ran out of fuel and crashed in various localities, including Jiangxi. NANCHANG, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- Eighty-four years after the first U.S. air strike on the Japanese home islands during World War II, family members of some of the airmen traveled across the Pacific to retrace mountain paths where Chinese peasants risked torture and death to shelter downed American flyers, and to honor a friendship forged in wartime. In Yangcun Village, Shangrao City of east China's Jiangxi Province, Thomas Macia first met 94-year-old Guan Dongxiang, who was still a short-haired little girl gaping behind an American pilot, Jack Sims, copilot of the Doolittle Raid's Crew No. 14, in a black-and-white photo. James Macia, Thomas Macia's father, served as navigator and bombardier in the same aircrew. When he was nine, Thomas first saw the photo in his father's album. In the spring of 1942, Guan's father, Guan Wenqing, and fellow villagers helped rescue Sims in nearby Miliang'ao Village. Days later, the pilot returned with a camera and took the photo. "There she is!" Thomas Macia exclaimed at the first sight of the silver-haired Chinese woman on Sunday, along with five others from the Children of the Doolittle Raiders. "I knew she existed. I had not met her before. The greatest thing is that she is a direct connection to 1942." RETRACING WARTIME RESCUE In April 1942, 16 U.S. bombers led by Lieutenant Colonel James Doolittle took off from the USS Hornet aircraft carrier to bomb Japan, in retaliation for the attack on Pearl Harbor. After the operation, 15 planes heading for a designated airport in east China's Zhejiang Province ran out of fuel and crashed in various localities, including Jiangxi. Chinese villagers risked their lives to rescue the parachuting airmen behind enemy lines and helped them evacuate to safety. Of the 75 airmen whose aircraft came down, 64 were brought to safety. The rescue came at a tremendous cost. Many locals were suspected of sheltering the Americans, and some were tortured or even killed by Japanese invading soldiers. After the raid, Japan launched a three-month campaign in May 1942 to destroy air bases, airports and other infrastructure in Zhejiang and Jiangxi, to prevent them from being used by Chinese or U.S. air forces. The invading Japanese troops also waged biological warfare by spreading cholera, plague and other diseases, resulting in massive civilian deaths. During a visit to Miliang'ao Village, Thomas recounted how his father landed in the mountains: "He could see off the top of the mountain, and he was hugging a small pine tree for the night to keep from sliding down." A visit to Dapai Mountain helped Thomas better understand his father's ordeal. "For me, to walk a little way up the hill ... I could imagine what my father did to know more exact information and the sense of what it looked like more than 80 years ago," he said. Gusty winds swept away his father's backpack and supplies as he parachuted down. Local villagers brought him eggs, honey and other food, and lit fires to dry his clothes. He was later escorted to the township government office, where he was reunited with other crew members. Thomas's father once pointed to a spot on a map and told his son that his life was saved by Chinese villagers, officials and soldiers, whom he remembered to his last breath. REDISCOVERING SHARED MEMORY Unable to return to China in his lifetime, James Macia kept the photograph with care. His son later made it his own mission to find the descendants of those lifesavers in person. In 2018, Thomas traveled to China for the first time and met Luo Shiping, a researcher with the Shangrao Anti-Japanese War Culture Research Association. The two have exchanged about 1,000 emails ever since. Over the years, Thomas combed through U.S. archives and provided clues, while Luo visited all crash sites and parachute landing areas across Shangrao, interviewed villagers and compiled investigation reports. After the war, Doolittle Raiders and their descendants established organizations such as the Children of the Doolittle Raiders. They hold annual commemorations, seminars and photo exhibitions to honor the Chinese who took part in the rescue. Researchers in Shangrao have continued to collect scattered documents and oral testimonies, working with their American counterparts to preserve this transnational memory. Their work has helped bring the heroic story to a wider audience. An exhibition on the rescue at Shangrao Museum has attracted almost 300,000 visitors since its opening in August 2025, according to museum curator Jiang Jinmin. On Saturday, the visiting Children of the Doolittle Raiders group toured the exhibition. Tom Johnson, son-in-law of Crew No. 14 pilot John Hilger, stopped now and then to snap photos of the displays. "Shangrao established and created this wonderful place of memory. It makes us know what they (Doolittle Raiders) accomplished," Johnson said. The delegation donated historical memorabilia to the museum, including fabric from the parachute used by James Macia, historical photos and relevant news clippings. ENDURING FRIENDSHIP On Saturday, the delegation also visited a 140-year-old residence in Fujia Village, where five members of Crew No. 14 posed for a group photo during the war. Tears welled up in Thomas's eyes as he entered the house. He had seen the airmen's group photo as a child. "I've been told for years that this (house) was destroyed. But here it is," he said. Fu Yuntuo, still a boy and a descendant of the house's former owner, approached Thomas and told him that his family elders had often told him stories about the American airmen who once stayed in the house. Friendship is the greatest bond in the world, Fu said. For Thomas, his connection with Shangrao extends beyond historical research. Whenever floods, earthquakes or other disasters strike southern China, including Jiangxi, he contacts Luo to ask whether the area has been affected. "The Doolittle Raid embodies Chinese and American elders fighting side by side against fascism through adversity for WWII victory," Luo said. "I will work with Thomas to pass the stories on to younger generations of both nations." ■ (Video reporter: Pan Xiaojing; Video editors: Pan Xiaojing, Zhang Nan and Zheng Qingbin)

item.title: Xi meets Togo's president of Council of Ministers, elevating bilateral ties to community with shared future for new era
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with President of the Council of Ministers of Togo Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, who is on an official visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 13, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping met with President of the Council of Ministers of Togo Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé in Beijing on Tuesday, during which the two leaders announced the elevation of bilateral relations to a China-Togo community with a shared future for the new era. Xi pointed out that the traditional China-Togo friendship was personally forged by leaders of an older generation of both countries, enjoying a solid foundation and growing ever stronger with the passage of time. China and Togo share aligned visions for friendly cooperation and enjoy broad prospects ahead, Xi said. Xi called on the two sides to further enhance exchanges at all levels between the two parties and the two countries, deepen the sharing of experiences in governance, and firmly support each other on issues concerning core interests and major concerns. China welcomes Togo to effectively utilize measures such as China's zero-tariff policy and the "green channel" for products exported to China, further enhance its role as a regional hub for trade and logistics, and facilitate the entry of more distinctive local and regional products into the Chinese market, Xi added. Xi noted that China appreciates Togo's efforts to expand the cross-border use of the RMB and is willing to strengthen cooperation with Togo in new energy, digital intelligence and other fields to support Togo's industrialization process. Noting that China and Togo share similar positions on international and regional affairs, Xi also called on the two sides to enhance multilateral coordination. Xi put forward four principles for the constructive participation of all parties in the settlement of hotspot issues in Africa. First, adhering to the principle of "Africa-led." The African people are the true masters of Africa and should play a central role in regional affairs, Xi said. Second, upholding fairness and justice. All participating parties should abide by the purposes and principles of the United Nations Charter and respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the countries concerned, he noted. Third, promoting ceasing hostilities for peace. Wars and unilateral sanctions cannot fundamentally resolve conflicts between countries. It is imperative to uphold mutual respect, conduct extensive consultations, seek common ground while shelving differences, and practice mutual understanding and accommodation. Fourth, addressing both symptoms and root causes. Efforts should focus on immediate security while planning for long-term development, Xi said. Faure, who is on an official visit to China, said that during his visit, he personally witnessed the remarkable achievements of Chinese modernization and the extensive promotion of fine traditional Chinese culture under the leadership of President Xi, and gained a deeper understanding of China's governance philosophy and the key to success. Noting that next year marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries, he said Togo is willing to enhance mutual trust with China, strengthen dialogue and communication, deepen enduring and mutually beneficial cooperation to jointly build a Togo-China community with a shared future for the new era, and better benefit the two peoples. The Togolese side fully agrees with the important principles proposed by President Xi for the constructive participation of all parties in the settlement of hotspot issues in Africa, Faure said. He expressed Togolese appreciation for China on its significant role in maintaining world peace and stability and jointly addressing global challenges, as well as the willingness to strengthen multilateral cooperation with China, jointly uphold multilateralism, and safeguard the interests of developing countries. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with President of the Council of Ministers of Togo Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, who is on an official visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 13, 2026. (Xinhua/Yue Yuewei)

item.title: China, Botswana establish comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan hold a welcome ceremony for Botswana's President Duma Gideon Boko and his wife Kaone Boko in the Northern Hall of the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 13, 2026. Xi held talks with Boko, who is on a state visit to China, after the welcome ceremony in Beijing on Tuesday. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- During their talks in Beijing on Tuesday, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Botswana's President Duma Gideon Boko announced the elevation of bilateral relations to a comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership. Noting that this year marks the 105th anniversary of the founding of the Communist Party of China and the 60th anniversary of Botswana's independence, Xi said the two countries' ruling parties should strengthen cooperation and deepen exchanges on governance experience. China supports Botswana in pursuing a development path suited to its national conditions, Xi said. He called on both sides to further improve the framework for economic and trade cooperation, and tap into new opportunities created by China's zero-tariff policy for African countries that have diplomatic ties with China. China is ready to strengthen cooperation with Botswana in the digital economy, agriculture, animal husbandry and other sectors, and to carry out the smart education project, Xi added. On promoting China-Botswana and China-Africa mining cooperation, Xi said Africa's resources belong to Africa, and this is the premise for cooperation. China is willing to share its own experience and help African countries formulate mining development plans tailored to their national conditions, and China will encourage Chinese enterprises to transfer green technologies suited to African conditions, Xi said. He said China will continue to promote China-Africa mining cooperation to move up the value chain and explore affordable, sustainable and innovative financing models. Noting that Africa's resources should not become a tool for geopolitical rivalry, Xi said China welcomes all parties' genuine contributions to Africa's development and stands ready to work with Africa to create a more enabling environment for investment and business operations. China has lifted all its poor population out of poverty and forged a successful development path with Chinese characteristics, from which Botswana has much to learn, Boko noted. He said that Botswana highly values its ties with China, and will firmly adhere to the one-China principle and oppose any separatist moves toward "Taiwan independence" and any external interference in China's internal affairs. Botswana is willing to strengthen development strategy alignment with China and welcomes more Chinese enterprises to invest and do business in Botswana, said Boko. He added that the country stands ready to maintain close coordination and cooperation with China, uphold multilateralism, strengthen the solidarity of developing countries, promote Africa-China solidarity and cooperation, and make the global governance system more inclusive and representative. After their talks, the two heads of state jointly witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents covering such areas as implementing the Global Security Initiative, Belt and Road cooperation, green minerals, health, and human resources. During Boko's state visit to China, the two sides issued a joint statement on establishing a China-Botswana comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership. Prior to the talks, Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan held a welcome ceremony for Boko and his wife Kaone Boko in the Great Hall of the People. Xi and Peng also held a welcome banquet for them in the evening. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Botswana's President Duma Gideon Boko, who is on a state visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 13, 2026. item.title: New bridge linking China, DPRK to facilitate trade, people-to-people exchanges: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
BEIJING, Oct. 14 (Xinhua) -- A new bridge across the Yalu River, the border river of China and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), will further facilitate trade and people-to-people exchanges between the two countries, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Wednesday. As agreed upon by China and the DPRK, the bridge will officially open to traffic on Thursday, with both sides jointly holding an opening ceremony on that day. China and the DPRK are friendly neighbors connected by mountains and rivers, and the new bridge is an important facility for connectivity between the two countries, Mao said at a regular press briefing. The bridge is expected to boost bilateral trade and people-to-people exchanges, and help improve the well-being of both peoples, she said. ■

item.title: China's consumer inflation ticks up on rising energy prices
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
BEIJING, Oct. 14 (Xinhua) -- China's consumer price index (CPI), a main gauge of inflation, rose 0.9 percent year on year in September on higher energy and industrial consumer goods prices, official data showed on Wednesday. On a monthly basis, the CPI increased 0.2 percent, with the growth rate narrowing by 0.2 percentage points from the previous month, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). In the first nine months of 2026, consumer prices rose 0.9 percent from a year earlier. The year-on-year increase in September was mainly driven by higher energy and industrial consumer goods prices, while falling food prices weighed on overall inflation, NBS statistician Dong Lijuan noted. Gasoline prices surged 16.6 percent year on year, contributing approximately 0.47 percentage points to the overall CPI increase, the data revealed. Prices of industrial consumer goods, excluding energy, rose 1.6 percent year on year, contributing about 0.39 percentage points to the CPI growth. Service prices increased by 0.8 percent, unchanged from August, contributing around 0.4 percentage points to the CPI increase. Travel-related service prices climbed 2.1 percent, while medical service prices were up by 4 percent. Food prices, meanwhile, fell 1.7 percent year on year, with the decline widening by 0.3 percentage points from August, dragging down the overall CPI by approximately 0.29 percentage points. On a month-on-month basis, higher prices of industrial consumer goods and food helped push up the CPI, while seasonal declines in travel-related service prices partly offset the increases, the NBS said. ■

item.title: China's foreign trade maintains sound momentum in first three quarters
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
The State Council Information Office (SCIO) holds a press conference on China's import and export of the first three quarters of 2026 in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 14, 2026. (Xinhua/Jin Liangkuai) BEIJING, Oct. 14 (Xinhua) -- China's foreign trade maintained sound momentum in the first three quarters of 2026, with both exports and imports growing rapidly and the overall growth rate reaching its highest level for the same period in five years, official data showed Wednesday. The country's total imports and exports rose 18.8 percent year on year to 39.94 trillion yuan (about 5.94 trillion U.S. dollars) in the January-September period, according to the General Administration of Customs (GAC). Growth accelerated through the year, with the expansion rate rising from 15.3 percent in the first quarter to 18.3 percent in the second quarter and 22.3 percent in the third quarter. Foreign trade growth in the first three quarters was the fastest for the same period in the past five years, with both quarterly and monthly growth rates generally accelerating, said Wang Jun, GAC's deputy head. "Latest international data show that such a growth rate ranks among the top among major economies, and China remains the world's largest trader of goods," the official told a press conference on Wednesday. Exports increased 16.4 percent year on year to 23.2 trillion yuan, while imports expanded by 22.3 percent to 16.74 trillion yuan, GAC data showed. In September alone, China's total imports and exports reached 5.16 trillion yuan, up 27.5 percent from a year earlier and crossing the 5-trillion-yuan mark for the first time. This figure also marked the sixth consecutive month of double-digit monthly growth. Exports rose 29.6 percent year on year to 3.03 trillion yuan, while imports grew 24.6 percent to 2.13 trillion yuan for the month. The country's trade with more than 180 countries and regions expanded during the first three quarters. Trade with free trade partners reached 19.55 trillion yuan, up 30 percent and contributing over 70 percent of the total trade increment. Meanwhile, trade with other APEC economies rose 23.9 percent to 24.07 trillion yuan. Trade with ASEAN grew 22.7 percent to 6.84 trillion yuan, that with the European Union rose 8.4 percent to 4.78 trillion yuan, and trade with the United States increased 4.1 percent to 3.18 trillion yuan. Exports continued to shift toward new and higher-quality growth drivers. The equipment manufacturing sector contributed nearly 90 percent of the export increment, while intermediate goods accounted for more than half of total exports, underpinning global industrial and supply chains, according to the GAC. ■

item.title: Xi sends congratulatory letter to 140th Canton Fair
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
BEIJING, Oct. 14 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday sent a congratulatory letter to the 140th edition of the China Import and Export Fair, which is also known as the Canton Fair. In his letter, Xi said over the past 70 years since its establishment, the Canton Fair has played a significant role in promoting trade exchanges between China and other countries, serving as an effective platform for China to expand high-level opening up and promote the building of an open world economy. Under the new circumstances, China is willing to join hands with countries around the world to safeguard the multilateral trading system, ensure the stability and smooth operation of global industrial and supply chains, expand the space for mutually beneficial international economic and trade cooperation, and promote a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, to inject new momentum into global development and prosperity, Xi said. The fair opened on the same day in Guangzhou, capital of south China's Guangdong Province. ■

item.title: Xi calls for decisive progress in Healthy China advancement
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, delivers an important speech during a national meeting on health in Beijing, capital of China. The meeting was held in Beijing on Monday and Tuesday. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has called for efforts to firmly follow a path with Chinese characteristics in developing the country's health programs, to secure decisive progress in the Healthy China Initiative over the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a national meeting on health held in Beijing on Monday and Tuesday. Xi stressed that people's health is a key benchmark of a nation's prosperity and strength. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, the Party has made a major decision to launch the Healthy China Initiative, promoting the establishment of the world's largest systems of medical services, traditional medicine, disease prevention and control, and healthcare security, said Xi, noting that the country has achieved historic accomplishments and made all-round progress in healthcare. In 2025, China's average life expectancy rose to 79.25 years, while its major health indicators remained at the leading position among upper-middle-income countries and countries with a population exceeding 100 million. Xi said the goal is to build a Healthy China, where health services are ensured in a balanced, inclusive, high-quality and efficient manner. Xi stressed that people's health should be factored into all policies and reflected in every aspect of work. Prevention, he said, is the most cost-effective and efficient approach to protecting public health. He called for greater emphasis on foundational health work, addressing risks at their source, and encouraging the public to adopt a sound understanding of health and take an active role in managing their own well-being. He also called for a stronger disease prevention and control system to guard against large-scale outbreaks. Xi underscored the need to optimize the functions and structural layout of medical institutions so that people can access medical care close to home and receive effective treatment. China has supported the development of 125 regional medical centers in areas where high-quality medical resources are relatively scarce. Notably, more than 90 percent of residents can access nearby medical and healthcare services within 15 minutes, while primary-level medical institutions account for over 50 percent of all medical visits nationwide. He also urged efforts to improve mechanisms for the preservation and innovative development of traditional Chinese medicine, strengthen basic research and original innovation in the health sector, and enhance the patient experience. Xi stressed that coordinating the development and regulation of medical services, medical insurance, and pharmaceuticals should be a key priority in reforming China's medical and healthcare systems. He also called for efforts to train and develop a sufficient number of highly qualified medical professionals. Efforts will also be made to actively promote the building of a global community of health for all, work with other countries to address major challenges in the health sector, and continuously improve the health and well-being of people around the world, he said. Other Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi attended the event. In his concluding remarks, Li Qiang said Xi's important speech provided guidance for advancing China's health sector. Li called for better coordination between improvements in public health and economic and social development, and urged deeper reform, innovation, opening up and cooperation, stronger prevention and control of major diseases, further development of a tiered diagnosis and treatment system, and greater use of science and technology to improve health services. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, delivers an important speech during a national meeting on health in Beijing, capital of China. The meeting was held in Beijing on Monday and Tuesday. Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi attended the meeting. The meeting was held here on Monday and Tuesday. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen)
